questions.question:
By interchanging which two signs the equation will be correct?

13 – 9 × 2 ÷ 3 + 16 = 3
questions.solution:
Given equation:- 13 – 9 × 2 ÷ 3 + 16 = 3

After interchanging two signs according to the options,

1) – and ÷

13 ÷ 9 × 2 - 3 + 16 = 3

1.45 × 2 – 3 + 16 = 3

2.90 – 3 + 16 = 3

18.90 – 3 = 3

15.90 = 3 False

2) – and ×

13 × 9 – 2 ÷ 3 + 16 = 3

117 – 0.67 + 16 = 3

133 – 0.67 = 3

132.33 = 3 False

**3) – and +**

**13 + 9 × 2 ÷ 3 - 16 = 3**

**13 + 6 – 16 = 3**

**19 – 16 = 3**

**3 = 3 True**

So, option 3 is true then no need to check the remaining option.

Thus, the correct answer is “- and +”.

questions.question:
The radius of a hemisphere is 14 cm. What is the cost of painting the outer curved surface of the hemisphere at the rate of Rs. 45 per cm²?

( {{{Take pi }} = {{ }}frac{{22}}{7}} )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of hemisphere = 14 cm.

**Calculation:**

Outer surface area of a hemisphere is 2πr²

So, outer surface area of hemisphere = 2 × 22/7 × 14² cm²

⇒ 1232 cm²

⇒ The cost of painting = 1232 × 45

∴ **The cost of painting the outer surface of hemisphere is Rs. 55440**

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 6 km/h. Time taken by the boat to cover a certain distance upstream is 3 hours more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, then what is the total distance (upstream and downstream) covered by the boat?
questions.solution:
Given, the speed of boat in still water is 6 km/hour

And the speed of stream is 2 km/hour

⇒ The speed of boat in downstream = 6 + 2 = 8 km/hour

And the speed of boat in upstream = 6 – 2 = 4 km/hour

Let the fixed distance be x km

Now, according to question

x/4 = 3 + x/8

⇒ x/4 – x/8 = 3

⇒ x/8 = 3

⇒ x = 24

⇒ The total distance covered by the boat in upstream and downstream = 24 × 2

∴ The total distance is 48 km

questions.question: E, F and G together can complete a work in 12 days and E and F together can complete the same work in 30 days. Then in how many days can G alone complete the same work?

Work done by E, F and G together in 1 day = 1/12

And, work done by E and F together in 1 day = 1/30

⇒ The work done by G in 1 day = 1/12 – 1/30 = 1/20

∴ The time taken by G to do the whole work is 20 days

questions.question: The proportion of the number of students in three classes is 1 : 2 : 3. If 20 students are included in each class, then the proportion becomes 3 : 5 : 7. What was initially the total number of students in the three classes?
questions.solution:
Let the ratio be x

So, number of students in three classes are x, 2x and 3x

According to question,

Increased number of students in three classes are (x + 20), (2x + 20) and (3x + 20)

And the given proportion of increased students is 3 : 5 : 7

So, are (x + 20)/ (2x + 20) = 3/5

⇒ 5x + 100 = 6x + 60

⇒ x = 40

So, the total number of student in the class initially = x + 2x + 3x

⇒ 6x

⇒ 6 × 40

⇒ 240

∴ The total number of students in the class initially was 240

questions.question: The area of a square is 144 cm². What is the perimeter of the square formed with the diagonal of the original square as its side?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The area of a square is 144 cm².

**Formula used:**

Area of square = (side)²

Perimeter of the square = 4 × side

**Calculation:**

Let the length of side of square be a cm

Given, the area of square = 144 cm²

So, a² = 144

⇒ a = 12

The length of diagonal = √2 × 12

⇒ 12√2 cm

The length of side of new square is 12√2 cm

The perimeter of new square is 4 × 12√2

**∴ The perimeter of new square is 48√2 cm.**

questions.question: What is the value of 16 ÷ 48 × 12 + 4 ÷ 8 × 16 + (7 - 2) × 25 ÷ 15?

Step-1: Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first and in the bracket,

Step-2: Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

questions.question: Vishal alone can complete 1/3 part of a work in 60 days and Ashok alone can complete 1/4 part of the same work 30 days. In how many days Vishal and Ashok together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Since, work done by Vishal in 60 days is 1/3 part of the work

⇒ The work done by Vishal in 1 day = 1/180 part of the work

⇒ The work done by Ashok in 30 days = 1/4 part of the work

⇒ The work done by Ashok in 1 day = 1/120 part of the work

⇒ The work done by Vishal and Ashok together in 1 day = 1/180 + 1/120 ⇒ 1/72

∴ The time taken by them to complete the whole work is 72 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Total time to complete the work by Vishal = 180 days 

Total time to complete the work by Ashok = 120 days 

Let total work be 360 units (l.c.m of 180 and 120)

Efficiency of Vishal = 360/180 = 2 units/day 

Efficiency fo Ashok = 360/120 = 3 units/day 

Efficiency of (Vishal + Ashok) = 5 units/day

⇒ The time taken by Vishal and Ashok together to complete the work is 

360/5

⇒ 72 days

**∴ The time taken by them to complete the whole work is 72 days.**

• The Lord Buddha was born in **563 BC** in the sacred area of **Lumbini**__ located in the Terai plains of **southern Nepal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Mahayana Buddhism:

 
 
• After the death of Buddha, a group evolved who believed that compassion for all humanity was an important part of the path, and that teaching is fully available to all.
 
• Those who followed the newly expanded ideals called themselves Mahayana meaning the big raft.
 
• In Mahayana Buddhism, all practicing Buddhists are apprentice Bodhisattvas.
 
• In Mahayana countries, images of the Buddha are set up in the temples and homes as an object of worship.
 
 
 
• Hinayana Buddhism:
 
 
• From about 100 years after the death of the Buddha, there had been a movement towards embracing the style of Buddhism.
 
• The early monks concentrated on personal enlightenment, seeking spiritual answers for themselves, and teaching others the way of enlightenment.
 
• But the information was severely limited to the lay community as it was assumed only minks could achieve Buddhahood.
 
• This section came to be known as Hinayana or also known as Theravada.
 
• Theravada means the way of elders.
 
 
 
• Milindapanha:
 
 
• The Milindapanha, or "Milinda's Questions," is an important early Buddhist text that usually is not included in the Pali Canon.
 
• Even so, the Milindapanha is cherished because it addresses many of Buddhism's most difficult doctrines with wit and clarity. 
 
• The Milindapanha presents a dialogue between King Menander I (Milinda in Pali) and an enlightened Buddhist monk named Nagasena.
 
• Menander- I was an Indo-Greek king thought to have ruled from about 160 to 130 BCE.
 
• He was a king of Bactria, an ancient kingdom that took in what is now Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan, plus a small part of Pakistan.

questions.question: Based on economic activities, how many sectors are there in Indian economy?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian economy can be classified into various sectors on the basis of ownership, working conditions and the nature of the activities.
 
• There are basically **three-sector** in the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector**: In the Primary sector of the economy, activities are undertaken by directly using natural resources. Agriculture, Mining, Fishing, Forestry, Dairy, etc. are some examples of this sector.

 
 
• It is called so because it forms the base for all other products. Since most of the natural products we get are from agriculture, dairy, forestry, fishing, it is also called Agriculture and allied sector.
 
• People engaged in primary activities are called red-collar workers due to the outdoor nature of their work.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector**: It includes the industries where finished products are made from natural materials produced in the primary sector. Industrial production, cotton fabric, sugar cane production, etc. activities come under this sector.
 
 
• Hence its the part of a country's economy that manufactures goods, rather than producing raw materials.
 
• Since this sector is associated with different kinds of industries, it is also called an industrial sector.
 
• People engaged in secondary activities are called blue-collar workers.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector**: This sector’s activities help in the development of the primary and secondary sectors. By itself, economic activities in the tertiary sector do not produce goods but they are an aid or support for the production.
 
 
• Goods transported by trucks or trains, banking, insurance, finance, etc. come under the sector. It provides the value added to a product the same as the secondary sector.
 
• This sector jobs are called white-collar jobs.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the provisions on Panchayat Raj Instiutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eleventh Schedule**__.

__
 
• **Eleventh Schedule** of Indian Constitution contains the provisions on **Panchayat Raj Institutions**.
 
• The **73rd Amendment 1992** added a new **Part IX** to the constitution titled **“The Panchayats”** covering provisions from **Article 243 to 243(O)**; and a new Eleventh Schedule covering **29 subjects** within the functions of the Panchayats.
 
• **Initially**, India’s constitution had **395 articles** in **22 parts and 8 schedules** at the time of commencement.
 
• **At present**, the Constitution of India has **448 articles in 25 parts, 12 schedules**.
 
• There are a total of **12 Schedules** in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Schedules

 
 
 
**Provisions**

 
 
 

 
 
First Schedule

 
 
 
List of States & Union Territories

 
 
 

 
 
Second Schedule

 
 
 
Salary of President, Governors, Chief Judges, Judges of High Court and Supreme Court, Comptroller and Auditor General.

 
 
 

 
 
Third Schedule

 
 
 
Forms of Oaths and affirmations

 
 
 

 
 
Fourth Schedule

 
 
 
Allocate seats for each state of India in Rajya Sabha

 
 
 

 
 
Fifth Schedule

 
 
 
Administration and control of scheduled areas and tribes.

 
 
 

 
 
Sixth Schedule

 
 
 Provisions for the administration of Tribal Area in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram & Arunachal Pradesh
 
 
 

 
 
Seventh Schedule

 
 
 
Gives allocation of powers and functions between Union & States. It contains 3 lists Union List, States, Concurrent List

 
 
 

 
 
Eighth Schedule

 
 
 
List of 22 languages of India recognized by Constitution

 
 
 

 
 
Ninth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains acts & orders related to land tenure, land tax, railways, and industries.

 
 
 

 
 
Tenth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of disqualification of grounds of defection.

 
 
 

 
 
Eleventh Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of Panchayati Raj.

 
 
 

 
 
Twelfth Schedule

questions.question: Who built the Hawa Mahal situated in Jaipur?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e __**Sawai Pratap Singh**__.

__
 
• **Hawa Mahal**, also known as **“Palace of Breeze”**, was built in **1799** as an extension to the Royal City Palace of Jaipur.
 
• In 1799, the Kachhwaha Rajput ruler, **Sawai Pratap Singh**__, grandson of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh ordered Lal Chand Usta to construct an extension to the Royal City Palace.
 
• The five-storeys palace was built in the form of Krishna’s crown because Sarai Pratap Singh was devoted to Krishna, the Hindu god.
 
• **Jaipur**, the current capital of Rajasthan, was built in 1727 AD by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II.
 
• Jaipur gained the name of Pink City in 1853 when Sawai Ram Singh ordered to paint all royal and government buildings in sandstone colour to welcome the Prince of Wales (later King Edward VII) to the city.

questions.question: Which part of brain maintains posture and balance of human body?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, __**Cerebellum**__.

 
• **Cerebellum,** part of the brain maintains posture and balance of the human body.
 
• **The cerebellum** is located behind the top part of the brain stem (where the spinal cord meets the brain) and is made of two hemispheres (halves).
 
• The cerebellum receives information from the sensory systems, the spinal cord, and other parts of the brain and then regulates motor movements.
 
• The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements such as posture, balance, coordination, and speech, resulting in smooth and balanced muscular activity.

questions.question: As per Article 274 of constitution, whose prior recommendation is required to the Bills affecting taxation?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct.

__
 
• **Article 274 in The Indian Constitution**: Prior recommendation of **President**__ required to Bills affecting taxation in which States are interested.
 
• In this article, the expression “tax or duty in which States are interested” means-
 
 
• A tax or duty the whole or part of the net proceeds whereof are assigned to any State.
 
• A tax or duty by reference to the net proceeds whereof sums are for the time being payable out of the Consolidated Fund of India to any State.

questions.question: Which type of reproduction occurs in hydra?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e __**Budding**__.

__
 
• **Hydra**__ can reproduce by **regeneration and budding**.
 
• Budding, in biology, a form of asexual reproduction in which a new individual develops from some generative anatomical point of the parent organism.
 
• In budding, initially buds appear as a small bulge, they further grow, and within 2-4 days they become fully-formed hydra.
 
• Then it detaches from the parent body.
 
• In regeneration, regrowth of damaged or lost part takes place.
 
• Hydra reproduces sexually and asexually both. Asexual reproduction takes place either by budding or by fission.
 
• Hydra belongs to Phylum **Coelenterata**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest peninsular river in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

__
 
• The **Godavari** is the **largest peninsular river in India**.
 
• The Godavari is one of the longest rivers in India and its total length is about **1,465 km**.
 
• The tributaries of the Godavari are **Purna, the Wardha, the Pranhita, the Manjra, the Wainganga and the Penganga**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Godavari River rises in northwestern Maharashtra in the Western Ghats range, only about **80 km from the Arabian Sea**, and flows for most of its course generally eastward across peninsular India.
 
• After traversing Maharashtra it enters **northern Telangana** and then **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The river then turns southeastward for the last 320 km of its course, flowing through a gap in the Eastern Ghats ranges and then across
 
• Andhra Pradesh state before reaching the Bay of Bengal.
 
• There it empties via its two mouths: the Gautami Godavari to the north and the Vasishta Godavari to the south.
 
• Rajahmundry is located on the banks of the River Godavari.
 
• Godavari river is also known as **Dakshin Ganga**.
